text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.2% today to $397.25, continuing a strong two-week rally that has gained 9.3%. The move comes as U.S. crude oil pulled back below $100 a barrel after a multiday rally, but refineries across the country are running at 97.8% capacity—near maximum levels—while gasoline and diesel inventories remain relatively lean. This tight operating environment supports margins for refiners like Marathon, even as crude prices moderate.

The backdrop remains volatile: Saudi Arabia shut down its East-West pipeline following multiple attacks, and Houthis have advanced toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments. These geopolitical pressures have kept crude prices elevated (Brent at $109.51), and the Iran war has injected further uncertainty into energy markets. With refineries maxed out and supplies constrained, Marathon benefits from the wider spread between what it pays for crude and what it sells refined products for—a dynamic that can persist even if raw crude prices fluctuate day to day.
